messages.author: cf90957368b0c5d2
messages.subject: RE : [unmarked] using predict function with model including offset for transect length
parts:
Hi Alejandro,

Both predict( ) in unmarked and predictSE.zip( ) in package AICcmodavg (>= version 1.35) produce the same prediction when using an offset. To illustrate what an offset does, you might want to experiment a bit with a Poisson distribution (instead of a ZIP).

When you are modelling an abundance as a rate (abundance per transect length for example), you are actually doing the following:

log(mu/transect.length) = linear predictor

log(mu) - log(transect.length) = linear predictor

log(mu) = linear predictor + log(transect.length)

Note that the linear predictor is the combination of beta estimates and explanatory variables forming the predictive equation.

Thus, if you want the predicted value of abundance for a given transect length, you have to exponentiate:

mu = exp(linear predictor + log(transect.length))

This is what happens with predict( ) and predictSE.zip( ) for a Poisson. For the zero-inflated Poisson, you must compute the linear predictor for the Poisson as above, but the final step involves:

mu = exp(linear predictor + log(transect.length)) * (1 - (exp(psi.pred)/(1 + exp(psi.pred))))

This is because the zero-inflated Poisson includes an additional parameter psi and its beta estimate is on a logit scale.

I suggest you work one of your examples using a simple model with only a single variable on abundance.

Hope it helps,

Marc M
